content.title: Freedom Park: Miami's new face as the city heads toward the 2026 FIFA World Cup
content.text: The countdown is on. Inter Miami CF is getting ready to open a new chapter as the next Major League Soccer (MLS) season kicks off at the club’s state-of-the-art stadium inside the ambitious Miami Freedom Park project. And as excitement builds on the field, major infrastructure upgrades are also moving forward—changes that promise to transform the fan experience from top to bottom. When will the stadium be fully finished? While the stadium will be ready for its debut on April 4, 2026, the broader project will be delivered in phases: Early 2026: opening of the stadium and the first sections of the park. Late 2026: significant progress on the park and the main public areas. Later phases: full buildout of the retail, hotel, and office district. Local In other words, fans will be able to enjoy soccer from day one, while the rest of the complex continues to grow around it. What other spaces will Freedom Park include? The Freedom Park development—located on the grounds of the former Melreese golf course near Miami International Airport—continues to take shape with the help of key state funding. It won’t be just a sports destination. A cornerstone of the project is a large public park intended to become a major new green “lung” for the city. Highlights include: A 58-acre public park: one of Miami’s largest, featuring trails, green areas, and recreational spaces. A large-capacity hotel: designed especially for travelers given its proximity to the airport. A retail and dining district: with shops, restaurants, and experiences for the whole family. Offices and a business hub: aimed at attracting investment and jobs. Event and concert spaces: turning the complex into a year-round destination. Flood mitigation: resources will be allocated to raise the land, improve drainage, and ensure the area’s long-term environmental sustainability. Easier access: special transportation for matchdays All of it is part of a more than $1 billion development that aims to bring sports, community, and tourism together in one place. Freedom Park will also have a new main roadway. A four-lane road spanning more than a mile will be built to make getting to the complex easier. With fan convenience in mind, the region’s rail system has announced special trains for weekend night matches. The service will connect directly to the station near the stadium (Intermodal), making access easier from different parts of South Florida. Although construction of a pedestrian bridge that would make the walk more direct is still pending, officials say the current route is walkable and safe. A project that goes beyond sports Since its initial approval in 2018, Miami Freedom Park has evolved into far more than a stadium. It’s a bet on urban development. Even though the stadium will not be an official venue for the 2026 FIFA World Cup (Miami matches will be played at Hard Rock Stadium), its impact will be significant. A strategic location: it sits next to the international airport, making it one of the first sights visitors will see. An alternative entertainment hub: it could host side events, fan zones, and World Cup-related activities. Improved mobility: connections like Tri-Rail will make it easier for thousands of tourists and fans to get around. In addition, MLS will pause during the World Cup, allowing all attention to focus on the tournament while the new complex is already up and running.
